context7_usage.reason: Pure repo-local spec turning the already-read B277 event taxonomy + envelope schema into fixture-driven smoke scenarios. No new external MCP-SDK/API/library question is open; server.py's existing FastMCP tool surface is only read, never modified.

builds_on: CLAUDE_TASK_MCP_OWNER_NOTIFICATION_LOOP_SPEC_B277_V1 (task_mcp_owner_notification_loop_spec_b277_v1.json -- 5-kind event taxonomy: completion, failure, stale, usage, duplicate_runner; envelope schema; caller-owned delta-cursor design; honest pull-not-push framing)

DEEPSEEK_TASK_MCP_AUTOLAUNCH_DRYRUN_SPEC_B276_V1 (task_mcp_autolaunch_dryrun_spec_b276_v1.json -- 4-gate safety model, dryrun-only launch templates, LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED=false invariant reused here to justify 'no subprocess model launch')

tools/aiworkhub/src/aiworkhub/server.py (current tool surface: aiworkhub_completion_inbox returns exactly 4 facets -- review_queue, stale_processing, runner_mismatch_warnings, latest_validation_facts; no error/exception facet exists today, confirmed by direct reading of the tool's docstring; unmodified by this task)
summary: This is a SPEC-ONLY smoke-test artifact (no code changes to server.py, completion_inbox.py, or any _.py module; no subprocess launches a model CLI; no live SQLite write). It turns B277's 5-kind event taxonomy into 6 fixture-driven smoke scenarios (completion, blocked, duplicate-runner, stale, usage, error) plus 2 edge cases (no-pending-task, tool_error-vs-failure disambiguation), each with an exact synthetic fixture, the expected classified event_kind, the exact envelope+payload the classifier should produce, and a deterministic owner-facing one-line summary template. Every scenario is a pure in-memory dict fed to the ALREADY-DEFINED B277 classification rule (lifecycle_state / validation_status / stale threshold / usage-record presence / collision_guard output) -- no new tool is registered, no live queue row is read or written, and no claude/codex/deepseek process is spawned anywhere in this spec.

section_0_scope_and_label_mapping.title: Scope + honesty note on card-wording vs B277 canonical enum
section_0_scope_and_label_mapping.canonical_event_kind_enum_unchanged: completion | failure | stale | usage | duplicate_runner (B277 section_2 envelope_schema.event_kind -- NOT modified by this task)

card_wording_to_canonical_mapping.blocked: failure -- this task card's word 'blocked' is an OWNER-FACING DISPLAY LABEL for B277's canonical 'failure' event_kind (trigger_condition: validation_status==FAIL or blocker_reason non-null, i.e. the task IS blocked). It is NOT a new enum value; no envelope.event_kind ever contains the literal string 'blocked'.
card_wording_to_canonical_mapping.error: tool_error -- a NEW smoke-test-only category, distinct from 'failure'. See section_2. Not added to the B277 envelope enum; exists only as a smoke-test assertion about how the (still unimplemented) delta tool must degrade when its READ SOURCE errors, not when a task's own validation fails.

section_0_scope_and_label_mapping.no_overclaim_note: This spec does not implement aiworkhub_completion_inbox_delta (still proposed-only per B277 section_2b) and does not add a 6th value to the event_kind enum in any executable code. 'error' is a smoke-test scenario category only, describing a required degrade-gracefully behavior for a FUTURE implementation task.

section_1_smoke_scenarios.title: 6 fixture-driven smoke scenarios, no live queue mutation, no model launch
section_1_smoke_scenarios.fixture_method: Each scenario supplies a synthetic in-memory task-card dict shaped like a taskctl JSONL row (or, for tool_error, a synthetic subprocess/JSON failure condition) and states the expected output of the ALREADY-DEFINED B277 classification rule. 'Smoke test' means: exercise every event_kind branch plus the disambiguating edge cases with a minimal, fast, deterministic fixture set -- not a live launch, not a load/stress test, not a real subprocess call.

fixture_condition.simulated_failure: taskctl subprocess (list/show) exits non-zero, OR its stdout is not valid JSON, OR task_queue_v1.sqlite is temporarily locked/unreadable

scenario_tool_error.source_facet: none -- the read source itself failed before any facet (review_queue/stale_processing/runner_mismatch_warnings/latest_validation_facts/usage_report/collision_guard) could be produced
scenario_tool_error.expected_event_kind: tool_error (NOT part of the B277 envelope enum; see section_0)
scenario_tool_error.expected_behavior: The (future, still-unimplemented) delta tool MUST catch the subprocess/JSON/sqlite exception, return a bounded error result (never raise past the MCP boundary, never crash the server process, never retry-loop indefinitely), and MUST NOT synthesize a false completion/failure/stale/usage/duplicate_runner event from partial or corrupt data.
scenario_tool_error.owner_facing_summary_template: The task-notification read source failed ({error_kind}): {error_message}. No task event could be classified this cycle; retry next loop iteration.
scenario_tool_error.owner_facing_summary_rendered: The task-notification read source failed (read_source_failure): sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked. No task event could be classified this cycle; retry next loop iteration.
scenario_tool_error.distinct_from_failure_note: This is explicitly NOT the 'failure'/'blocked' event_kind: 'failure' means a WORKER's task validation failed (a row with real data exists, its validation_status is FAIL). 'tool_error' means no row could be read at all -- the classification pipeline itself broke, so the owner is told about a plumbing problem, not a task problem.

section_2_tool_error_definition.title: Why 'error' needed a 6th category instead of folding into 'failure'
section_2_tool_error_definition.rationale: Folding a read-source crash into 'failure' would make a task_id show up with validation_status=FAIL when the real problem is that taskctl/sqlite could not be read at all -- an owner acting on that event would investigate the WRONG task's validation instead of the plumbing. Keeping tool_error separate (task_id=null, no source_facet) makes the distinction visible in the payload shape itself, not just in prose.
section_2_tool_error_definition.not_implemented_anywhere: No server.py tool, no completion_inbox.py facet, and no exception-handling code exists for this today. All four completion_inbox facets in the current codebase (review_queue, stale_processing, runner_mismatch_warnings, latest_validation_facts) let taskctl subprocess/JSON errors propagate uncaught; this is recorded as an open gap and next-wave item, not fixed by this spec.

no_pending_task.title: Empty-queue edge case (acceptance requirement)
no_pending_task.expected_behavior: Zero events emitted. The (future) aiworkhub_completion_inbox_delta call returns {events: [], next_cursor: <unchanged-or-advanced-per-B277-section_2b>, counts: {by_kind: {}}, truncated: false, authority_flags: {...all false...}}. This is NOT an error condition and must NOT be classified as tool_error -- an empty queue is a valid, successfully-read state with no notifications to raise.
no_pending_task.owner_facing_summary_rendered: No pending task-notification events for this topic/cursor.

duplicate_runner_conflict_detail.cross_reference: see section_1_smoke_scenarios.scenario_duplicate_runner for the full fixture+payload; this edge case entry only re-confirms the acceptance requirement that duplicate-runner is a covered scenario, not a second design.

section_4_owner_facing_summary_index.rendering_rule: Plain Python str.format() over the exact payload field names in section_1 -- no external templating library, no LLM-generated summary text, deterministic and reproducible byte-for-byte given the same payload.

section_5_authority_flags.title: Authority Flags (ALL FALSE, same shape as B277 section_4 plus no new flags)

neural_bridge_note: This spec introduces no learned decision authority and no regex/keyword cue router: every scenario's event_kind is a fixed 1:1 mapping from an already-recorded fixture field state (mirroring the B277 deterministic mapping) to one of 6 taxonomy labels -- a deterministic support-boundary/evidence-extraction mapping used only to validate a future read-only tool's classification correctness, not a routing or intelligence decision. Owner-facing summary rendering (section_4) is plain str.format(), explicitly not an LLM call, so it introduces no new neural surface either. If a future task teaches a controller to PRIORITIZE, DEDUP, or NATURAL-LANGUAGE-SUMMARIZE these events beyond the fixed templates, that becomes a neural curriculum target per neural_bridge_priority; this task only defines the deterministic smoke-test shape.
